scenarios.desc: Did staged changes touch security-critical files
scenarios.input: I am about to commit. I staged .github/workflows/deploy.yml and src/Controllers/AuthController.cs. Did I touch security-critical files, and do I need the security agent to review? Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: Detected Patterns lists .github/workflows/* as Critical (Review Required) and **/Controllers/** as High (Review Recommended). The two risk levels are the distinguishing output.

scenarios.desc: Run the detector on staged files
scenarios.input: How do I check my staged files for infrastructure and security-critical changes before committing? Name the script and the flag. Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: Usage section gives python detect_infrastructure.py --use-git-staged and --files. A generic answer would not name that script.

scenarios.desc: Classify a mixed file list by risk level
scenarios.input: Which of these need a security review: .husky/pre-commit, infra/main.tf, certs/server.pem, docs/readme.md? Give each a risk level. Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: Detected Patterns puts .husky/* and *.pem in Critical and *.tf in High. A markdown doc matches neither list, so the output is No infrastructure/security files detected for it.

scenarios.input: Scan my Python source for command injection patterns such as shell=True with interpolated strings before I submit. Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: The description says Detection only. Do NOT use to scan source for injection patterns (use security-scan). This skill matches file paths, not code content.
